top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation is a single chemical principle, recruitment of an E3 ligase into a ternary complex for catalytic, event-driven removal of a chosen protein, reproduced independently for about twenty-five years. P001 (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) gives the most coherent citation: Crews and Deshaies for the PROTAC concept and first proof of principle, Handa for identifying cereblon as the thalidomide target, which underlies the glue strand and most clinical degraders. P003 (Ciulli instead of Handa) is the same discovery but would leave the glue strand without a named discoverer, so it is second. P002 (Buchwald, Hartwig) is a mature, well-defined method but a sequel to the 2010 cross-coupling prize with a Kosugi priority question, so I rank it third, still above no award.
